articleTitle: Microwave Imaging over UWB with Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna for Concealed Weapon Detection
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: An Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna (AVA) is presented here for microwave imaging applications. To start with, a conventional AVA is designed for reference, and then periodic slit edges or corrugations in the form of sinusoids are furnished at the edges to obtain the desired performance for microwave imaging applications. The proposed antenna achieves high bandwidth from 1.2 – 14 GHz with a peak gain of 13 dBi at 10 GHz with a matching better than 15 dB from 3 – 14 GHz. The proposed antenna will be used for the detection of a concealed gun with different clutter removal algorithms applied to obtain its precise image.

articleTitle: Microwave Breast Imaging using Synthetic Aperture Radar Method utilizing UWB Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: This work describes an Ultra-Wideband (UWB) antipodal antenna utilized for the microwave imaging of a breast phantom. The designed antenna consists of stubs arraged at a particular length apart to widen the bandwidth and an elliptical patch at the aperture of the structure is placed to improve the performance at high frequencies. The proposed antenna achieves a bandwidth from 1.3 GHz to around 14 GHz with good impedance matching as well. The designed antenna attains a peak gain of 10 dBi at 6 GHz and the proposed structure is utilized for the monostatic microwave imaging of the breast with two tumors using Synthetic Aperture Radar.

articleTitle: Human Movement Recognition System Using CW Doppler Radar Sensor with FFT and Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: This paper presents a novel human movement recognition system using continuous-wave Doppler radar and deep learning with convolutional neural networks. The proposed monitoring system using Doppler sensor has environmental robustness, dark/light-independence, and are privacy-protected unlike traditional cameras. It works at a distance and does not cause discomfort to the elderly and patients.The proposed system was evaluated with various types of deep learning, including VGG-19, AlexNet, and GoogleNet CNNs (convolutional neural networks). The better performance of the monitoring system reaches 94.29% accuracy using VGG-19 CNN for detecting activities like falling, stopping, jumping, walking, and crouching. The Doppler radar sensor is inexpensive and an alternative to consider when the privacy of the elderly and patients is necessary. The proposed monitoring system of the elderly and patients can be used in an IoT (Internet of Things) network with multiple Doppler sensors scattered around the environment.

articleTitle: A Simple Low-Profile Broadband Antenna Design for 5G Millimeter-Wave Applications Over 38 GHz Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: A broadband antenna operating over 36.8 - 43 GHz frequency range is proposed in this paper for 5G wireless communications systems. The antenna design is extracted from circular patch antenna by loading three patches between circular radius and feed-line. Further improvement in antenna's performances is achieved using a perpendicular pair of elliptical slots inside the circular patch. The proposed antenna offers compact size of 12 mm x 15 mm x 0.79 mm and covers the globally allocated band spectrum for 38 GHz communication systems with more than 7 dBi gain and 90% radiation efficiency throughout the working frequency area. The antenna has designed and analyzed using Higher Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS). Furthermore, a comparison with state-of-the-art-works is performed to show the potential of proposed design for targeted frequency band. The results confirm that, the proposed antenna with advantages of small size, wide bandwidth, resonance frequency with high impedance matching at 38 GHz, high radiation gain and efficiency, low cost, and simple geometry is a proper candidate for 5G millimeter-waves applications.

articleTitle: Transmitter and Receiver Equalizers Optimization for PCI Express Gen6.0 based on PAM4
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: The continuously increasing bandwidth demand from new applications has led to the development of the new PCIe Gen6, reaching data rates of 64 GT/s and adopting PAM4 modulation scheme. While PAM4 solves the bandwidth constraint in high-speed interconnects, it brings new challenges for the physical channel analysis. Equalization (EQ) plays an important role even with PAM4 signaling. PCIe specification defines requirements to perform EQ at the transmitter (Tx) and at the receiver (Rx). During the EQ process, one combination of Tx/Rx EQ coefficients must be selected to meet the performance requirements of the system. Testing all possible coefficient combinations is prohibitive. Current industrial practice consists of finding a subset of combinations at post-silicon validation using maps of EQ coefficients. Finding this subset of coefficients is time-consuming, along with all the new challenges imposed by PAM4. In this paper, we propose an optimization approach for PCIe Gen6 link EQ. Our proposal is based on a suitable objective function formulated over the channel operating margin (COM), which is a new figure of merit (FOM) adopted by standards of communications for signaling speeds beyond 25 Gbps.

articleTitle: Optimizing a Buck Voltage Regulator and the Number of Decoupling Capacitors for a PDN Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: An optimization methodology to determine the best values of the compensation elements of a buck voltage regulator (VR) as well as the optimal number of decoupling capacitors in a power delivery network (PDN) application is proposed. A state average equivalent circuit model of the buck converter is employed. The proposed optimization methodology gradually finds the best compensation parameter values of a buck converter VR to meet some stability criteria in a PDN application. Additionally, the number of parallel decoupling capacitors in the PDN is minimized to simultaneously meet a frequency-domain impedance profile specification and a time-domain voltage droop requirement.

articleTitle: Microwave Sensor Based on Split Ring Resonators for Dielectric Characterization of Density and Viscosity of Milk
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: This article presents a multi-resonant sensor (double band) that uses open ring resonators (SRR) to detect milk adulteration with water. The sensor has a dual resonant frequency of 2.5GHz and 3.5GHz using an industrial, scientific and medical (ISM) band. This sensor was implemented on Rogers substrate using a single port. The process of detecting milk adulteration (i.e. milk with water) was performed by immersing the sensor in different samples. With the displacement in resonance frequency a numerical model was developed that allows relating the physical characteristics of the milk, which were mass density and viscosity with the dielectric characteristics of the milk. The proposed sensor is of low cost, easy implementation and manipulation.

articleTitle: On the Optimum Number of Antennas for V2V LOS Links with Ground Reflection
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: This paper investigates the rate of improvement of a vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) line-of-sight (LOS) communication link with respect to the density of antennas used at each vehicle. The objective is to find a trade-off between system complexity and communication performance considering that the link is affected by multiple ground reflections (self-interference). The antennas are assumed to be located at regularly distributed positions across the surface of contiguous vehicles. The work assumes symbol repetition at the transmitter side, and different signal combining mechanisms at the receiver side, namely maximum-ratio and equal-gain combining (MRC and EGC, respectively). The main objective of the optimization investigated here is to minimize the outage probability of the LOS link affected by multi-ray ground reflections (calculated over a range of inter-vehicle distances) with respect to the free-space loss case. The results show that performance is improved even for a relatively small number of antennas and that a critical point is reached beyond which improvement is only differential. This suggests that an optimum trade-off can be obtained to ensure a value of outage probability with a complexity constraint over a range of inter-vehicle distances.

articleTitle: Optimization of an array of smart antennas using PSO for the monitoring of electrical power switches
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)

authors.preferredName: A. F. L. Alves da Silva
R. J. F. P. V. de Almeida

abstract: This work proposes the use of the Particle Swarm Optimization method (PSO) to maximize the main beam of an intelligent, switched array of four Yagi-Uda antennas. The antenna feeds, amplitude and phase, are the PSO input variables, which not only maximizes the main lobe for a given direction, but also minimizes all secondary ones. The MATLAB software is used to make the simulations. Radiation patterns are here produced, which show that PSO is efficient for maximizing lobes in the range from 0° to 180°. Suggestion of an arrangement for a 360° coverage around the array is also presented.

articleTitle: Non- invasive Serum Glucose Sensing Using a Double U-slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: Diabetes is a chronic disease where the body does not produce sufficient insulin hormone to control glucose levels. To prevent health complications arising, diabetics must continuously monitor their blood glucose. Currently, blood glucose levels are mainly monitored using invasive methods which can discourage regular testing. This paper proposes a non-invasive double U-slot patch antenna system to monitor blood glucose levels. COMSOL was used to simulate the port impedance and resonant frequency shifts for varying glucose blood vessel concentrations. The impact of sensor placement, relative to the blood vessel, on glucose level sensitivity was explored considering the relationship between blood glucose concentration and RF-based predictors. Results demonstrate that the lumped port magnitude resonant frequency shift correlates with the range of glucose concentrations investigated. The sensitivity is better at lower frequencies for the designed sensor, and the sensor is relatively insensitive to rotation shifts and horizontal shifts, while vertical shifts, representing more fatty tissue impact the sensitivity.

articleTitle: Design of a Doherty Power Amplifier with GaN Technology in the Sub-6 GHz Band for 5G Applications with Harmonic Suppression
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: This paper shows the methodology for the design of a Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA), based on a well stablished non linear model for a GaN device, complemented with a harmonic suppression network. For 30dBm input power we got 18% of improvement in efficiency with respect to the conventional Doherty configuration. This design can be useful for 5G applications in the Sub 6GHz band.

articleTitle: A High Power Ku- to Ka-Band Single-Pole-Double-Throw Switch with Capacitive Loading for Isolation Improvement
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: In this paper, we report a design of single-pole-double-throw (SPDT) passive high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) switch using stacked-FET configuration with capacitive loading for isolation improvement. Based on the analysis subject to the insertion loss and isolation, devices with proper gate peripheries were selected for the realization of the SPDT switch. Implemented in commercial 0.15-μm GaAs pHEMT technology, the proposed design showed an insertion loss of less than 3 dB with an isolation greater than 30 dB from Ku-band up to Ka-band frequencies. Moreover, the SPDT switch achieved a nice power handling capability of better than 31.5 dBm across 26–40 GHz.

articleTitle: A Swarm Intelligence based Automated Framework for Variability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: In this paper, a novel methodology for variability analysis of CMOS circuits is presented. An automated framework is proposed that uses swarm intelligence based optimization technique, namely particle swarm optimization algorithm, to estimate the worst-case variability bounds of the system response. The efficacy of the proposed method is illustrated by performing the variability in phase noise of a 2.4 GHz CMOS LC tank RF oscillator. The proposed methodology is investigated and validated by comparing it with the conventional Monte Carlo simulations technique. For this case study, the proposed method is found to be significantly time-efficient.

articleTitle: Application of thin dual-band electromagnetic absorbers to reduce the radar cross section of a microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: In this paper, a thin microwave electromagnetic absorber based on a high-impedance surface is proposed in order to serve as a ground plane for a square patch ISM microstrip antenna. While the bottom layer is fully grounded, preventing any transmission of waves, the top layer is made of periodic, metallic double square rings that reflect waves within the two antenna working bands. Simulations yield scattering parameters, which are then used to obtain the absorptivity, permittivity and permeability of the absorbing structure. In the best scenario tested, the absorber is capable of reducing the radar cross section of the antenna by more than 10 dB in both its bands, namely 12.3 dB at 2.45 GHz and 16.2 dB at 5.65 GHz.

articleTitle: Simulation and Fabrication of a Low-Cost RFID Reader
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: RFID (Radio-Frequency Identification) systems have their importance renewed due to the surge of the Internet-of-Things scenario. This article describes the design and fabrication of a low-cost RFID Reader. This research comprises the fabrication of a printed antenna of the reader, as well as generating the waveform used in the transmission as a proof of concept. The antenna is designed on ANSYS HFSS and then printed on a FR-4 substrate using microstrip lines. The waveform is designed as a set of sinusoids and then generated on Labview. The setup is validated as a proof of concept using an indoor scenario, with passive RFID printed tags placed 50 cm from the reader. The received waveforms present an adequate signal level.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of a Simple and Wideband Antenna for 5G mm-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: An 8.5 GHz wideband and high Gain cross elliptical shape antenna is presented in this paper for the 5G mm-wave applications. A short-pin opposite to the feeding arm is deployed for the maximum current flow and consequently high bandwidth ranging from 26.7 to 35.2 GHz is achieved. The gain of the antenna varies from 6.1 dBi to 8.47 dBi in the entire frequency range with more than 76% efficiency. The compact electrical size of the antenna is 0.89λ0 × 0.89λ × 0.14λ0, where λ0 corresponds to the free space wavelength at the lowest resonance frequency. The results are compared with the state-of-the-artwork for the 5G mm-wave applications.

articleTitle: Orthogonal Polarized Horn Antenna with High Port Isolation at Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: Orthogonal Polarized Horn Antenna with high port to port isolation at millimeter wave frequencies is presented. WR-34 waveguide is used as feed at two ports for horn antenna. Dual-polarization with good port to port isolation is achieved by using redesigned Magic-T structure in the feed horn. The simulated results show that the port isolation is more than 60 dB and the gain is 16dB for both ports at 28GHz. The Proposed dual polarized antenna is modelled using HFSS 3D EM software. Simulated results on radiation pattern, gain and frequency response of S-parameters at two ports are presented.

articleTitle: Comparison of Measured and Predicted Permittivity Values for 3D Printed PLA Substrates
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: The resultant relative permittivity of 3D printed polylactide (PLA) substrates with varying percentage volumes of PLA are measured using a two microstrip line method. The resultant relative permittivity of the PLA substrates is also predicted using five existing heterogenous mixture models. The measured and predicted values of relative permittivity are compared to identify the degree of fit of the mixture models to the measured values. The measured relative permittivity was found to increase as the percentage volume of PLA was increased. The measured values also increased with increasing signal frequency. The mixture models showed varying degrees of fit with two models, Rayleigh (RAY) and Refractive Index (RI), showing the best fit out of the five models. None of the models considered the frequency dependence of the relative permittivity. The results allow for the identification of opportunities for future work related to frequency dependent mixture models and detailed testing of 3D printed substrates.

articleTitle: Nonlinear current source model for a GaAs transistor implemented in Verilog-A using pulsed measurements
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: A Verilog-A model for a GaAs MESFET was implemented and validated. A modified nonlinear equation for Ids shows good results in the modelling of DC and pulsed I–V measurements. Transient simulations were performed, showing some of the dispersive effects in RF transistors due to the presence of traps.

articleTitle: Design of Half Power Divider at Ku-band using Empty Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: This paper presents a half power divider operating at Ku-band which is designed using concept of Empty SIW. For easy connectivity with other planar microwave devices and circuits, the micro strip line to HSIW transition was implemented, with section of ESIW expanded at discontinuity interface, to reduce radiation and leakage effects and provide impedance matching. An ESIW based, half power divider is fabricated on RT/duroid 5880 and measured in range of 11.5 GHz to 18.5 GHz. This power divider provided a return loss of at least 12 dB, an insertion loss of 0.5 ± 0.03 dB, and also when used as Power combiner, its power combining efficiency is observed as 89.4% from 12–16.5GHz.

articleTitle: Modeling Power Supply Induced Jitter in a Voltage-Mode Driver with Long Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: Power Supply Induced Jitter (PSIJ) is one of the major stakeholders in the timing budget of high-speed systems. In this paper, a systematic methodology for estimation of PSIJ for high-speed circuits having long transmission lines is presented. A semi-analytical approach considering both the spatial and temporal components of the long lines is used and the corresponding equations are derived for a voltage-mode driver circuit. The analysis is validated by comparing the proposed methodology with the conventional approach to estimate PSIJ while inducing different types of noise on power supply.

articleTitle: Optimization of Branch-Line Hybrid Couplers for Ku-Band Applications in SIW Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: This paper presents an in-line optimization process for the design of branch-line couplers in Ku-band, using Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) technology with microstrip transitions. This optimization process uses a link between CST Microwave Studio and Matlab, the formulation of objective functions, and the Nelder-Mead optimization algorithm, which made it possible to obtain optimal designs in the waveguide and SIW technology, with couplings around 3 ± 0.88 dB and isolations lower than 20 dB and a phase difference of 90 ± 2° between the output ports, for the frequency band between 14.0 GHz and 16.0 GHz; and all with a reduction of around 14 % of the computation time required when compared with the optimizer of the CST program.

articleTitle: A Compact Ultrathin Metamaterial Absorber for C, K and Ka Band Microwave Frequency Regime
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: In this paper, focus is on development of polarization independent absorber having broad angle of incidence, low profile and compactness in microwave frequency range. The unit cell focuses to achieve maximum absorption at C, K and Ka band. The structure is simulated and the results are analysed for different angle of polarization and angle of incidence. The dimensions of structure are ultrathin and compact with 8mm×8mm×0.8mm. The dimensions are optimised in such a fashion to achieve three different peaks at three different microwave bands i.e. C, K and Kaband. The proposed structure after optimization provides peak absorption of 98.49%, 91.1%, and 96.9% at C Band, K and Ka band of microwave regime, respectively.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of broadband UHF microstrip meander antennas for an RFID reader
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: This article presents the design of Ultra High Frequency (UHF) broadband microstrip meander antennas for Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) with possible application to Internet-of-Things scenarios. Two antenna models are proposed with two different types of feeding, one with coaxial feed and the other one with Y junction. Simulation results show an omnidirectional characteristic, adequate beamwidth and low value for S11 parameter.

articleTitle: A Type of Multi-Notched-Band Microstrip Crossover
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: A class of planar crossover with embedded multi notched bands is presented. It is based on a multi-stage-branch-line-type crossover with one-port split-type multi-notched-band filtering cells that are connected at all its ports. The theoretical principles of the proposed co-designed crossover/multi-notched-band RF device are detailed for the dual-notched-band case. Moreover, for practical-validation purposes, a microstrip prototype of triple-notched-band crossover is developed and tested, in which a compact-size one-port coupled-multi-line interdigitaltype triple-notch filtering stage is exploited as split-type cell. It exhibits optimized crossover performance between its two first notches in terms of input-power-matching and power-isolation levels between non-connected ports—i.e., 1.69–2.27-GHz spectral range—with an additional upper out-of-band notch at 2.84 GHz.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Three Types of VHF/UHF Antennas for GPR Array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: This article presents the comparative analysis of antennas for Ground Penetration Radars (GPR) that operate in the VHF/UHF band around 200 MHz. Three types of antennas are optimized to improve bandwidth, obtain a gain greater than 5 dB while analyzing their Half Power Beam Width-HPBW, and front to back levels. These antennas are candidates to be implemented on a 2×2 array for a double polarized GPR to improve its resolution and range. This radar conducts non-invasive explorations to obtain data from Caral’s archaeological center in the city of Lima, Peru. The geometry design, simulation results, and optimization of the antennas were calculated using the ANSYS-HFSS software. The simulation results have indicated that the Antipodal Vivaldi antenna showed better results than the Log Periodic Dipole Arrays and the DGS Vivaldi antennas.

articleTitle: A 17 – 32 GHz Wideband High Isolation Linear mm-Wave Mixer For 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: An mm-Wave novel RF mixer with folded cascode Topology along with double balanced switching configuration that is designed in 130 nm Technology is presented. The proposed mixer uses current folding cascade topology for achieving high isolation between the RF and LO port, and an improved bandwidth (BW). Moreover, it has used source degeneration inductor in order to achieve high linearity and providing input matching over the wideband. The proposed mixer produces more than 21 dB of conversion gain (CG), less than −10 dB of input matching (S11), more than 65 dB of RF-LO isolation, and the third-order input intercept point (IIP3) of 11.5 dBm for the frequency ranges of 17 – 32 GHz.

articleTitle: Use of the Stimulated Brillouin Scattering Effect in Optical Fibers to Generate Microwave Signals
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: Stimulated Brillouin Scattering (SBS) effect present in single-mode optical fibers is used to generate microwave signals. This approach is carried in an experimental way obtaining the microwave signal around 11 GHz exhibiting a Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of 45 dB. Afterward, by means of a series of simulations using the VPI photonics software, it is demonstrated that this frequency can generate harmonic frequencies at 21.99 GHz and 32.98 GHz. For this goal, a Mach-Zehnder Intensity Modulator (MZ-IM) acts as a frequency duplicator obtaining the harmonic signals of 21.99 GHz and 32.98 GHz. SNR values for both signals produce 36.58 dB and 20.45 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: A Wide Bandwidth Hybrid Filter Based on Discrete Acoustic Resonators
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: In this work, a hybrid filter based on acoustic wave resonators is shown. The filter uses lumped elements to increase the effective electromechanical coupling factor of the acoustic wave resonators. The simulation results show that a hybrid topology could be used in 5G frequency bands that require a fractional bandwidth over 25%.

articleTitle: Capabilities of LiNbO3 Based Acoustic Wave Resonators for Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: Acoustic Wave technologies have been traditionally the most suitable solution to microwave filters for end-user applications due to the reduced size and high performance. However, standard technologies are not able to face new released 5G bands due to inherent limitation in the achievable bandwidth. Functional materials as LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> operating in particular modes with specific cut and rotation angle can overcome such limitation. This paper explores the main characteristics of this material using multiphysics 3D simulations and provides rule of thumbs for an optimum design.

articleTitle: FPGA-SoC based S-band Radio Frequency power amplifier control
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: Radio Frequency power amplifiers such as the one used decades ago for the S-band (2.9 GHz – 3.1 GHz) 2.5 MW peak power output Twystron can be rescued, modernized and used today, replacing many of their digital controllers with a simple Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) or FPGA System on Chip (FPGA-SoC). Starting with the inspection and description of the devices to be controlled, simulating their behavior, implementing hardware description language, adding the necessary peripherals and measuring at the system test points, this work tests that hypothesis and the experimental results are shown. This alternative represents not only an economic saving, but also the possibility of training and experimentation by converting an outdated system into one with a digital interface, greater reliability and greater adjustment options.

articleTitle: Phased Array with 45° Scanning and Over 65dB Polarization Purity from 53–100GHz Using PCB Flip-Chip Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: Use of the millimeter wave spectrum is essential for the success of 5G and beyond communications. Modern millimeter wave arrays suffer from bandwidth limitations due to dielectric loadings. In this paper, the latter is compensated with a higher order Marchand balun in each element of a tightly coupled dipole antenna array (TCDA). The array operates from 53–100GHz at boresight with a VSWR < 2. When scanning 45° from broadside in the E and D-planes a VSWR < 3 is maintained, and the same holds for up to 30° in the H-plane. The array has an impressive cross-polarization purity of over 65dB across the bandwidth. Moreover, the array exhibits over 84% efficiency across the band. It is designed and fabricated on Tachyon ISO 100 and copper features are within commercial PCB limitations. Furthermore, the array is designed for flip-chip technologies and in a triangular lattice for 15% phase shifter count reduction.

articleTitle: High-Performance Planar Hexagonal Coil-Type Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: This paper presents a high-performance planar hexagonal coil-type wireless power transfer (WPT) system based on strong magnetic coupling resonance. The antenna, possessing a 48-by-44 sq. mm area, acts as the resonating element. The proposed WPT has been developed on Rogers RO3003 substrate and operates at 433 MHz. Subsequently, the designed system demonstrates an extremely high power transfer efficiency (PTE) of more than 90% at a 23 mm distance. Furthermore, the WPT system provides more than 50% PTE during vertical and horizontal 18 mm misalignment shift. In addition, the WPT can provide more than 40% PTE when transmission distance varies from 23 to 36 mm.

articleTitle: Asymmetric Doherty Power Amplifier at 60 GHz in 130 nm BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: This work presents an asymmetric Doherty power amplifier in 130nm BiCMOS technology for the IEEE 802.11ad/ay Wi-Fi standard at 60GHz. An analysis of the baseband signal indicates a peak-to-average power ratio of 8dB, which has to be taken into account for an energy efficient operation. In laboratory measurements the power amplifier achieves a peak output power of 11.5dBm with a maximum power added efficiency of 20% at peak and 12% at output backoff level. In addition, a power gain of 22dB within 8GHz bandwidth was measured.

articleTitle: Error quantification for the design of a TCR-type passive calibrator for SAR applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: Trihedral corner reflectors (or TCR) are widely used as passive calibration targets for SAR imagery. This work focused on the quantification of several causes of error to be taken into account during the design and construction phases of a target of this type. The characterization was made using FEKO electromagnetics software, to simulate multiple configurations and to later quantify the losses due to the different sources of error. With the results it was possible to establish design tolerances for a TCR of fixed inner length, which will be useful in the subsequent construction process, and they showed potential for more comprehensive studies using a similar methodology.

articleTitle: Biasing Control and Protection System for GaN HEMT Power Amplifier Measurements
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: Depletion mode transistors, such as GaN HEMTs, are widely used in high-power RF applications. High-power RF amplifiers using GaN HEMTs are biased with large drain-source voltage, and a high current flows during its operation. Proper control of large voltage and current require precise biasing sequence and protection circuits for a reliable operation. In this study, a compact system to bias and protect high-power amplifiers is presented. It also has monitoring and data logging features. The system controls biasing sequence to turn the amplifier on/off, monitors the drain voltage, drain current, gate voltage, temperature, reflected or transmitted power, and protects the amplifier against overcurrent, high RF power, and high temperature. A microcontroller manages the biasing sequence, sensors, user interfaces, and settings. In addition to a keypad, monitoring and controlling is possible with a computer and Android device. The system is tested and verified with a 10W GaN HEMT power amplifier.

articleTitle: BPFET-based RF electronics: state-of-the-art, small-signal modeling and amplifier design
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC 2020)
abstract: Black phosphorus (BP) field-effect transistors (FET) have been proposed as a two-dimensional channel device technology able to operate in radiofrequency (RF) applications. A revision of the high-frequency figures of merit of fabricated BPFETs is provided here. Experimentally-calibrated small-signal models of state-of-the-art RF BPFETs have been used to design single- and double-stage amplifiers at 2.4 GHz. Results show that BPFET-based amplifiers are strong candidates for low-power high-selective RF systems.
